EXTENSIONS OF THE VECTOR-VALUED HAUSDORFF-YOUNG
INEQUALITIES
OSCAR DOMINGUEZ AND MARK VERAAR
Abstract. In this paper we study the vector-valued analogues of several in-
equalities for the Fourier transform. In particular, we consider the inequalities
of Hausdorﬀ–Young, Hardy–Littlewood, Paley, Pitt, Bochkarev and Zygmund.
The Pitt inequalities include the Hausdorﬀ–Young and Hardy–Littlewood in-
equalities and state that the Fourier transform is bounded from Lp(Rd, | · |βp)
into Lq(Rd, | · |−γq) under certain condition on p, q, β and γ. Vector-valued
analogues are derived under geometric conditions on the underlying Banach
space such as Fourier type and related geometric properties. Similar results are
derived for Td and Zd by a transference argument. We prove sharpness of our
results by providing elementary examples on ℓp-spaces. Moreover, connections
with Rademacher (co)type are discussed as well.

Extensions of Pitt’s inequalities have been studied in many papers. Below we
mention only some of them. A version for more general orthonormal sequences has
been obtained in [Ste56]. Versions of Pitt’s inequality with more general weights
and generalized Fourier transforms have for instance been studied in [BH03,BHJ87,
DCGT17, Hei84, LT12, SW90, GIT16]. There is special interest in the sharp con-
stants C in (1.1) and (1.3) in mathematical physics (see e.g. [Bec75,Bec95,Bec08,
Bec12, Eil01, Her77, Yaf99] and references therein). In particular, there is a con-
nection with the uncertainty principle and with Hardy-Rellich estimates which are
used in the theory of elliptic PDEs.
In this paper we will study vector-valued analogues of Pitt’s inequality. The
special case β = γ = 0 and q = p′ ≥2 is extensively studied in the literature. It
turns out that even in this special case (1.3) does not hold if f takes values in an
arbitrary Banach space X. In [Pee69] Peetre states that a Banach space X has
Fourier type p ∈[1, 2] if (1.3) holds for β = γ = 0 and q = p′. It turns out that this
notion becomes more restrictive if p is larger, and if p = 2 this property characterizes
Hilbert spaces (see [Kwa72]). Fourier type has been used in many parts of analysis.
For instance in interpolation theory [Pee69,CS88,SW06], Fourier multiplier theory
[BK05, GW03, Hyt04, RV17], evolution equations [ABHN11, CT03, RV18, WW96],
and geometry of Banach spaces [HNVW16,HNVW17,Pie07,PW98].

Theorem 1.1 is stated for Banach spaces with nontrivial Fourier type. It is well
known that many Banach spaces satisfy this assumption. For example the following
conditions are equivalent
(a) X has nontrivial Fourier type;
(b) X is B-convex;

(d) X has nontrivial (Rademacher) type;
(e) X has nontrivial Walsh type.

• Section 2 contains several preliminaries on interpolation and duality.
• In Section 3 we deﬁne the notions of Fourier, Paley and Hardy–Littlewood

Abstract: In this paper we study the vector-valued analogues of several in- equalities for the Fourier transform. In particular, we consider the inequalities of Hausdorﬀ–Young, Hardy–Littlewood, Paley, Pitt, Bochkarev and Zygmund. The Pitt inequalities include the Hausdorﬀ–Young and Hardy–Littlewood in- equalities and state that the Fourier transform is bounded from Lp(Rd, | · |βp) into Lq(Rd, | · |−γq) under certain condition on p, q, β and γ. Vector-valued analogues are derived under geometric conditions on the underlying Banach space such as Fourier type and related geometric properties. Similar results are derived for Td and Zd by a transference argument. We prove sharpness of our results by providing elementary examples on ℓp-spaces. Moreover, connections with Rademacher (co)type are discussed as well. Contents
